item.title: UCF football, Arizona State battle for bowl eligibility: Preview, predictions
item.description: ORLANDO — Every football team in the Big 12 is just about on level pegging, UCF head coach Scott Frost believes. That holds particularly true with regard to the Knights and their next opponent, Arizona State . UCF and Arizona State , which makes its first trip to the Acrisure Bounce House at 3:30 p.m. Saturday, share identical 5-4 records with 3-3 conference marks. Their offenses and defenses average similar scoring figures, and both teams have cycled through multiple quarterbacks due to injury — as well as inefficiency in Arizona State's case. "You guys agree it's all pretty close watching the games this year? I hope you do," Frost rhetorically asked during his press conference earlier in the week. "You've got to play well that week. Turnovers become even more important, and penalties and playing a clean game. The biggest differentiator, to me, is quarterback play." In that department, the two teams could not be further apart as it pertains to experience. Redshirt senior Alonza Barnett III helped James Madison reach last year's College Football Playoff and then transferred to UCF. Arizona State counters with freshman Jake Fette , set to make his third career start. Can the Knights keep things rolling and clinch bowl eligibility? The News-Journal's trio of Chris Boyle, Chris Vinel and Ken Willis share their thoughts and predictions. UCF vs. Arizona State tale of the tape Barnett returned to the Knights' starting lineup and engineered a clutch, go-ahead drive in the final minute. He capped it with a 6-yard touchdown pass to Caden Piening with one second left on the clock, and Will Stone booted the decisive PAT in a 33-32 win, snapping UCF's 12-game road losing streak that dated back to September 2024. UCF troublingly squandered a 19-point lead over the final 25 minutes. A month earlier, the Knights allowed 27 unanswered points at Houston after going ahead 17-0 in the third quarter. Josh Derry caught eight passes for a season-high 143 yards and a touchdown. The Knights' defense recovered a pair of fumbles, improving the team's takeaway total to 14 for the year — tied for 25th in the Football Bowl Subdivision. Fette became the first Arizona State quarterback to catch a touchdown pass since Jake Plummer in 1996. In his second career start, he completed 13 of 19 attempts for 187 yards and a touchdown against Colorado. Cardae Mack, another first-year Sun Devil, rushed for 80 yards. Reed Harris, the Big 12's leading receiver, caught four balls for 104 yards and a touchdown. Owen Long made 17 tackles as Arizona State's defense limited its third consecutive opponent to under 100 rushing yards. The Sun Devils alternated wins and losses through each of their nine games, and they have gone 1-3 away from home. item.title: Joe Hendry Part Of New WWE Tag Team Pitch (WWE News)
item.description: WWE.com WrestleVotes Radio on Fightful Select 's sources tell them that WWE bosses tasked "a handful of staff members" with scheming a soft overhaul of the tag-team divisions across both Raw and SmackDown "at one point over the summer". Staff weren't given any "brand restrictions", and were "encouraged to think outside the box and explore a wide range of possible combinations in an effort to bolster a somewhat lacking division". Tag wrestling, at least on the main roster, has been in a dire state for too long now. Indeed, it feels like it was the summer of 2025 when Triple H last really focused on doubles action. Since then, we've witnessed several nothing reigns and tag formations, such as R-Truth teaming with Damian Priest . More recently, Penta and Je'Von Evans combined to take the World Tag belts away from Vision duo Bron Breakker and Austin Theory at Crown Jewel in Saudi Arabia . For context, that was The Vision's first title defence, and it came almost 4 months after they'd won the belts on Raw! Perhaps the most interesting thing about this WrestleVotes/Fightful write up is that Joe Hendry's name was originally mentioned "numerous times" by WWE staff. There's apparently huge interest in turning the Scot into a tag success within the promotion. That'll be something to keep a watchful eye on as we roll towards 2027 and WrestleMania 43 season. Could buddying up with another worker be the way Hendry cements his place on Monday nights? Or, will he move to Fridays on SmackDown and win tag gold there? item.title: Oregon has 3 quarterbacks who could start Saturday. Illinois has a freshman who's never started before
item.description: The Oregon Ducks will face a team on Saturday with an even less desirable quarterback situation. Illinois (3-3, 1-2 Big Ten) quarterback Katin Houser suffered a broken hand that will sideline him for four to six weeks during a 38-37 overtime win over Michigan State on Oct. 10. Oregon has played its last two games without starting quarterback Dante Moore, who suffered a concussion in the second quarter of the Ducks’ 41-27 win at USC on Sept. 26. However, while Oregon can turn to junior Dylan Raiola — a Nebraska transfer with 23 career starts — and senior Brock Thomas, Illinois is relying on freshman quarterback Michael Clayton II, who will make his first start against the Ducks. A positive for Illinois is that Houser was injured before the team’s bye week, giving coach Bret Bielema two weeks to prepare Clayton. “It was just good timing,” Bielema told reporters during his Monday media session. Illinois is off to a disappointing start after going 9-4 in 2025 and 10-3 in 2024. The defense is below average, while the passing combination of Houser and wide receiver Collin Dixon is one of the nation’s best. Dixon is tied for third nationally with nine touchdown receptions. Illinois head coach Bret Bielema celebrates their overtime win over Michigan State as he walks off the field after an NCAA college football game, Saturday, Oct. 10, 2026, in East Lansing, Mich. (AP Photo/Lon Horwedel) AP Photo/Lon Horwedel AP Photo/Lon Horwedel Now Illinois heads into Saturday’s game against a resurgent Oregon defense, trying to get Clayton up to speed. His performance against MSU elevated expectations. Houser left the game late in the third quarter with Illinois leading 23-10. Clayton completed 6 of 8 passes for 88 yards and two touchdowns. The final touchdown came in overtime on a 25-yard pass that put Illinois up 38-31. Sophomore quarterback Carson Boyd also played. He rushed once for seven yards but did not attempt a pass. Bielema and offensive coordinator Barry Lunney Jr. both said Boyd could play against Oregon (4-2, 2-1), but Clayton is the starter. Usually, Bielema said, his starting quarterback gets a lot of rest during the bye week while the staff works on player development. Given Clayton and Boyd’s inexperience, both got valuable reps in practice last week. “I think those two guys in particular took advantage of every rep,” Bielema said. Bielema has leaned heavily on transfer quarterbacks during his six years at Illinois, including Houser. But that could change if Clayton, a former three-star recruit, earns the job. “I’ve said several times that hopefully the next starter comes from within our program,” Bielema said. Lunney said Clayton will be more prepared than he has in the past given the circumstances. item.title: 10 takeaways from Oregon’s loss at Illinois and firing of OC Drew Mehringer
item.description: CHAMPAIGN, Ill. — The Oregon Ducks (4-3, 2-2 Big Ten) suffered their worst loss of the season at Illinois on Saturday . The 21-10 defeat came against a marginal Illinois team that started a true freshman at quarterback, rushed for 225 yards, and held Oregon to two scoring drives. As a result, on Sunday, Oregon coach Dan Lanning announced the firing of offensive coordinator Drew Mehringer . What that means for the rest of the season remains to be seen. Mehringer had to contend with several key personnel issues, including starting quarterback Dante Moore missing three games while in concussion protocol. Here are 10 takeaways from Saturday’s game and the firing of Mehringer: 1. It feels like Mehringer is the scapegoat in this mess Criticizing play-calling is an armchair quarterback’s delight, but doing so under Oregon’s current circumstances is somewhat obtuse. Few teams excel without their starting quarterback. The next factor is an offensive line that was clearly mismanaged in the offseason after losing three starters to the NFL. Next is inconsistent play from backup quarterbacks Dylan Raiola and Brock Thomas. Then sprinkle in losing top wideout Jeremiah McClellan (broken foot) after three games, starting wide receiver Evan Stewart (undisclosed injury) for the last two games, and two more rotational wide receivers heading into Illinois. Does all of that excuse Mehringer for Oregon scoring just 42 points over the past three weeks? No. But those are a lot of obstacles for any offensive coordinator to overcome. Watch " Oregon football fires offensive coordinator Drew Mehringer " on YouTube Watch 2. Where does Lanning go from here? Lanning will probably announce his new offensive coordinator during his Monday press conference. He could promote from within to get through the season and then conduct a national search in the offseason. Or he may have someone in mind to take over now and beyond. Whatever Lanning decides, the next play-caller had better hope Moore returns, or little will change. 3. It could be time to add a veteran coach to the staff Lanning did well by hiring younger offensive coordinators, Kenny Dillingham and then Will Stein. But maybe it’s time to bring in an accomplished, seasoned veteran coach to add a new perspective to a relatively young staff. Someone with a track record of success as an offensive coordinator and maybe as a head coach. Someone like former Oregon coach Chip Kelly, Northwestern’s offensive coordinator. No, don’t expect Kelly to want to return to Oregon. But someone like him could fit perfectly. 4. The wide receiver situation After Saturday’s game, Raiola was asked twice how difficult it was to build timing with the receiving crew, which lacked McClellan, Stewart, and freshmen Messiah Hampton and Jalen Lott. item.title: Reeling Oregon Ducks remain positive, committed to the grind
item.description: EUGENE — The 2026 season is on the verge of completely unraveling for the Oregon Ducks . One more loss, and any shred of postseason hopes would be extinguished. Yet even after two upset losses and falling out of the rankings — despite starting the season at No. 2 — the Ducks (3-2, 1-1 Big Ten) remain focused, together and committed to salvaging the season. “One thing I really love is the way the people in the locker room have been responding to this adversity,” sophomore cornerback Brandon Finney Jr. said. After his team’s 17-15 loss to No. 12 UCLA on Saturday, Oregon coach Dan Lanning said the team would be measured by how it responds moving forward. On Wednesday, he said the team has elevated its work ethic and embraced accountability. “I’ve been proud of the way that they’ve worked,” Lanning said. “I don’t see a lot of hanging heads, right? I think that’s challenging, too, especially when you’re young, to not lose a little bit of gusto and not lose a little bit of belief.” Oregon linebacker Devon Jackson (#9) drops UCLA running back Wayne Knight (#3) for no gain as the No. 13 Ducks face the No. 21 Bruins in a Big Ten college football game at Autzen Stadium in Eugene on Saturday, Oct. 10, 2026. Sean Meagher/The Oregonian The Ducks, who host Nebraska (5-1, 2-1) at 8 p.m. Saturday, responded well to adversity following a 39-31 loss at Oklahoma State on Sept. 12. Oregon won its next two games, including a 41-27 win at USC on Sept. 26. That victory seemed to give the Ducks a fresh start. But two weeks later, they lost to the Bruins and dropped out of the rankings. Now, Oregon must run the table to have a legitimate shot at the College Football Playoff, which seemed like a given for a team that returned most of its starters from last year’s semifinal squad. He added that the team’s goals remain attainable, and team leaders have worked to encourage togetherness and mutual trust. “If you can’t trust your teammate, then everything ain’t going to form in the way that it’s supposed to,” he said. item.title: Oregon QB Dante Moore ruled out for rest of 2026 season
item.description: Oregon Ducks quarterback Dante Moore will miss the rest of the season, coach Dan Lanning announced Monday night. “I’m not anticipating him being back this season,” Lanning said. “Really got clarity for us this past week, for him,” Lanning added. “And I think if it were up to Dante in any shape, way, he would want to be out there playing for the guys. But, unfortunately, it’s not really up to Dante. It’s not really up to me. We can control the setting and practice where he’s able to do things for us, but that’s not always the case in the game.” Lanning said he expects Moore, who has run scout-team offense in practice, to fully recover. “That hasn’t changed,” Lanning said. “Definitely feel that way, but for him to be out there on the field for us right now, that’s not gonna happen.” Lanning added that Moore would remain involved with the team. “He’s still going to be a big part of this team and helping us move forward and find opportunities for us to be better,” Lanning said. Watch " Oregon Ducks QB Dante Moore to miss remainder of 2026 season " on YouTube Watch The announcement comes days after the reeling Ducks lost 21-10 at Illinois on Saturday in the third straight game Moore missed while in concussion protocol. Before the Illinois game, Moore told The Oregonian/OregonLive that he felt good but didn’t know if he’d return this season and was taking it “one day at a time.” “That’s all I can do,” he said. He then began throwing passes on the field in shorts and a sweatshirt. Saturday’s loss all but knocked Oregon (4-3, 2-2 Big Ten) out of the national playoff picture and led Lanning to fire offensive coordinator Drew Mehringer on Sunday. Without Moore, Oregon scored 42 points over three games and lost twice while rotating between backup quarterbacks Dylan Raiola and Brock Thomas. item.description: A new head coach will roam the sidelines. A franchise icon will make his long-awaited return. An All-Star will begin his redemption tour. And a new ownership group will watch its first season opener from Paul Allen’s former seats along the Moda Center baseline. The Blazers open the 2026-27 NBA season Wednesday night against the Phoenix Suns — a team they upset in April in the play-in tournament — and if you’re just now tuning in for the start of the regular season, well, there’s a lot you missed. RELATED: Suns vs. Blazers predictions, odds and best bets: Dame is home, and the model likes Portland on opening night Let’s catch you up. What does the starting lineup look like? The Blazers are expected to unveil a new starting lineup that features a pair of notable All-Star additions: Damian Lillard and Ja Morant . The backcourt duo is joining a fivesome that includes returning starters Deni Avdija , Toumani Camara and Donovan Clingan . It’s a versatile, star-studded lineup that features three All-Stars, a former All-Defensive Second Team selection, one of the best young centers in the NBA and loads of scoring potential. What about the rotation? Micah Nori , the Blazers’ first-year head coach, said he plans on using a 10-man rotation to start the season, which will allow the Blazers to capitalize on their depth and versatility. In addition to the starters, Jrue Holiday, Scoot Henderson, Sidy Cissoko, Robert Williams III and Vit Krejci are expected to open the season in the rotation. The group could change depending on matchups and Williams’ availability — he did not play in back-to-backs last season — and it’s likely that Micah Potter, Branden Carlson and Yang Hansen will occasionally see spot duty, as well. Wait … the Blazers have a new coach? The Blazers stabilized their turbulent coaching situation in June, hiring longtime NBA assistant Nori to replace interim coach Tiago Splitter . Nori, who interviewed for head coaching jobs seven times before finally landing his first chance, is entering his 29th season in the league and is universally revered in NBA circles for his positive approach, ability to connect with players and sharp basketball mind. Early indications have been encouraging, as the Blazers players seem to love him and the front office works well with him. The Blazers’ coaching position had been embroiled in controversy, of course, as former coach Chauncey Billups — who was placed on indefinite leave by the NBA — is facing federal felony charges related to money laundering and wire fraud conspiracy for his alleged involvement in a rigged underground poker game. What style will the Blazers play? In a stark contrast to recent seasons, the Blazers are constructed around their offense rather than their defense. item.description: Magic Johnson attends the 2024 NWSL Championship match at CPKC Stadium. © IMAGN Veteran center Nikola Vucevic has surpassed former NBA player and Lakers legend Magic Johnson on the all-time scoring list. The Orlando Magic center has played off the bench this season as he builds chemistry with a new squad. Meanwhile, fans on social media reacted in varied ways to the new update. Although Vucevic is averaging just 2.7 points and 2.8 rebounds this season, his points tally reached 17,714, surpassing Johnson, who scored 17,707 career points. Legion Hoops shared the update on X: “Mind-blowing fact: last night, Nikola Vucevic passed Magic Johnson on the NBA’s all-time scoring list.” Fans reacted to the update and shared their thoughts on social media, as one wrote: “Magic is low and vooch is underrated” Vucevic, who has played on four teams (two stints with the Magic) over 16 seasons and was an All-Star in 2018-19 and 2020-21, is slowly finding his spot back on the team he played for in his formative years. Meanwhile, the Magic (4-7) have struggled while the face of the franchise, Paolo Banchero, has been sidelined due to a low-grade right high-ankle sprain. Magic Johnson, a Hall of Famer who won three MVPs and five NBA championships, played 12 full seasons before retiring in November 1991 after testing positive for HIV. He returned for 32 games in 1995-96. Often running the star-studded Lakers, Johnson wasn’t relied upon solely for scoring. He averaged a relatively low 19.5 ppg, but holds the NBA record for assists per game at 11.19. He also led the league in assists four times and steals twice. The Magic look for rhythm after their first consecutive win this season Orlando has failed to find solid footing this season with Paolo Banchero nursing an ankle sprain. However, Franz Wagner has done all he can to keep the team afloat when they are short-handed, leading the offense with 23.5 ppg and 7.9 apg. Meanwhile, Anthony Black has emerged as one of the dark horses, as the team has looked better with him on the court. Averaging 17.8 ppg, 6.0 rpg and 5.5 apg, he makes a lot of difference with his activity and energy. The Magic won their last two games, as Black scored 26 against the Sacramento Kings and 22 against Utah. He grabbed seven rebounds and dished eight assists in an all-around performance. item.title: OSU's Legree leads nation in receiving as WSU clash looms
item.description: CORVALLIS — There may be no more appropriate way to describe Oregon State’s outrageously successful passing game this season than explosive. The Beavers lead the country in passing yards thanks in large part to 10 passes of 40-plus yards. Jesse Legree is responsible for eight of those catches, including all five of OSU’s 50-yard pass plays this season, making it no surprise that he leads the country in receiving yards and touchdowns entering this week’s matchup with Washington State. “You see him with ball in space, obviously taking the top off a number of times,” Washington State coach Kirby Moore said. “I think it’s about playing team defense. Obviously communication is going to be really important, where he’s at.” The Cougars (1-5, 0-2 Pac-12) have the No. 2 defense in the Pac-12 thus far and are having that success by keeping the top on their pass coverage. WSU has allowed 11 passes of 30-plus yards, which is tied for 129th nationally and nearly 10% of the passes it has allowed. However, opponents are not breaking through that mark often, with just four passes over 40 yards and none for more than 50, one of 30 teams yet to allow such a play this season. “We don’t want to let the verticals up,” Washington State safety Jaylen Smith said. “We take pride in (not) letting deep balls go. We always look to play top down and take away the deep routes first.” WSU defensive coordinator Trent Bray will be tasked with doing what nobody has been able to do yet this season: contain Legree. OSU offensive coordinator Mitch Dahlen has been creative in moving Legree around to prevent defenses from taking him away. Last week against San Diego State that included moving Legree into the backfield for a variety of plays. “People are going to try and hit him at the line of scrimmage,” Dahlen said. “They’re going to try and two-hand jam. Following the No. 1 Gamecocks’ 65-44 victory over the Tigers on Thursday, the star forward delivered a blunt response when asked whether she considers the matchup a rivalry. The result extended South Carolina’s winning streak against Clemson to 16 consecutive games, highlighting the gap between the two programs in recent years. When reporter Jared Parker asked Kitts in a press conference if she considers the matchup a rivalry, the Gamecocks star didn’t hesitate with her response. “Um… no, sir,” Kitts replied. item.description: From Indonesia to San Siro: Rudy's story 19 January 2011. It's a cold evening in Milano: winter is in full swing and temperatures at San Siro are hovering around freezing. Inter are playing Cesena in a rearranged Serie A Matchday 16 fixture which had been postponed due to the Nerazzurri's participation in the Club World Cup. Outside the gates, a young Inter fan is trying to get into the Meazza for the very first time. But our story begins a few years earlier in Purbalingga, a city on the Indonesian island of Java. Surrounded by tropical habitats and mountains, the city lies at the foot of Mount Slamet, one of the island's tallest and most prominent volcanoes. It is here that Ngudiono Prasetyo, known to everyone as Rudy, was born and raised. As a child, Rudy developed a deep love of football, playing with his friends whenever and wherever he could. Seeing his passion for the game, his sister decided to give him a present: an Inter shirt. The connection was instant. Rudy fell in love with the Nerazzurri colours and began following Inter, quickly becoming a devoted fan. One day, while watching a match on television, Rudy made a promise to himself and his friends: "One day, I'll be there, in that stadium, cheering on Inter, the team I love." Around 11,400 kilometres separate Purbalingga and Milano as the crow flies. That's roughly 24 hours of travelling, and by no means a cheap journey. But Rudy was determined to keep his promise. He dreamed of watching Inter play in person. And that's how we get to the night of 19 January 2011, his first in Milano. The night his dream came true. Let's fast forward to the present day. Rudy is now a grown man, and Inter remain a huge part of his life. He no longer lives in Indonesia, having moved to Townsville, Australia, not far from Brisbane. item.description: Glastonbury took the Class LL championship during the CIAC Girls Cross Country Championships held Saturday, October 31, 2026 at Wickham Park in Manchester. (Jim Shannon/Hearst Connecticut Media) When you talk about high school girls cross country in Connecticut, Glastonbury gets mentioned pretty often, and with good reason. This season, the Guardians won both the Class LL and State Open team championships, while junior Lauren Parrett claimed the individual titles in both races. Glastonbury earned its first state championship in 2004 in Class LL. Since then, the Guardians have won 13 more Class LL team championships, 14 overall. The program won its first State Open team championship in 2007, on the heels of a fourth straight Class LL title. The Guardians have captured eight State Open team championships. On 11 occasions, a Glastonbury runner has won a Class LL individual state championship. A Guardian has claimed the State Open individual title five times. Since 2004, the program has had an individual or team state champion in 17 of 23 seasons. What makes Glastonbury cross country successful So the question is, why is Glastonbury so good? "We do have a lot of good runners who have come through," said Parrett after she won the State Open on Nov. 5 at Manchester's Wickham Park. "I think a big part of it is us supporting each other all the time. I think it's our training, too." Parrett added: "We do a lot of training leading up to this, and we work hard for the positions and awards we get." Parrett is just one of multiple star runners who have come through the program. When talking about Parrett, head coach Brian Collins mentioned some of those other big names. They included Lindsay Crevoiserat, Kristin Mitchell and Brooke Strauss. More on all of them later. "As a freshman, I think (Parrett) was ninth in New England. She ran some good times here in her freshman and sophomore years," Collins said. "You don't know how much better some of these kids will get. Sometimes they stabilize because it's hard at that point." This is where Collins started to explain how the program reaches a championship level. "We're a low-mileage school. We do 29, 30, 31 miles a week," Collins said. "(Parrett) goes off in another program and does 35, 40, 45 miles a week, would she be a little bit stronger and better? Yes. We don't do that because at that point, the risk of injury is greater at that age. "People always think that we're running 40, 45, 50 miles a week. Our kids don't. If you do the workouts the right way, whether it be the harder days, the long-run days, the easier days or whatever, we found something that worked for us over the last 22, 23 years. item.title: Ospreys say report shows Wales must not cut teams
item.description: Ospreys now play home games at St Helen's [Huw Evans Picture Agency] Ospreys says a report they commissioned into Welsh rugby concludes that the proposed cut of four professional clubs to three should not happen. The Welsh Rugby Union (WRU) has said it intends to drop a side by 2028, with the decision made by next summer. With Cardiff and Dragons set to be granted the capital and east licences, Ospreys and Scarlets are competing to be the side in west Wales. Ospreys asked experts at Sheffield Hallam University to look at the issues and they produced the "Welsh rugby data report". That found "the independent analysis of the data does not logically lead to a conclusion that the removal of one professional team in Wales is a strategic move grounded in evidence". Ospreys say they back the need to keep four clubs. The report has not yet been published in full. That will not be done until later this month when it will be sent to the regions and WRU. Why four clubs should be maintained The Ospreys highlight the reasons the report concludes the number of professional clubs in Wales should remain at four. Derbies: The report claims fixtures between the four Welsh clubs generated 48% of league attendances at home games in Wales from 2012 to 2026. With three clubs, those fixtures would fall from 12 derbies a season to six. Players: Removing one team would create what the report calls a "bottleneck", with fewer elite playing opportunities in Wales and a greater risk of more Welsh players moving to clubs outside Wales. Wales: The report finds that Wales have recorded higher Six Nations finishes in the seasons when the Welsh clubs have performed well. All four clubs contribute: Over the period the report records Cardiff with the highest average attendances, Scarlets as the leading Welsh club in the European Cup and Dragons with the highest stadium utilisation, alongside the Ospreys' record in the league and in supplying most players to Wales and the Lions. What has not been included in great depth in the initial findings are the financial constraints or how keeping four teams can be afforded. The WRU has reported recent losses of £18m and says it has to reduce its spend on professional rugby from £26m to £20m by 2028. The four sides currently receive about £6.5m each. The Ospreys report follows the Keystone report that was commissioned by the WRU who said it outlined data why Welsh rugby needs to cut a side. item.title: Matt Henry and Will Young dismantle India as New Zealand register 244-run win
item.description: New Zealand kept the series alive with a commanding 244-run win over India in Friday's fourth one-day international at Mount Maunganui, driven by a century from Will Young and a six-wicket haul by Matt Henry, who dismissed the touring side for 89. Although trailing 2-1 in the five-match contest and unable to claim an overall series victory, the home team can still secure a draw should they win Sunday’s final fixture at the same ground. Rain had forced the abandonment of the third game. Set a target of 334, India endured a terrible start when fast bowler Henry reduced them to 0-3 during a devastating opening over, dismissing Rohit Sharma , Virat Kohli and Shreyas Iyer in quick succession. Ruturaj Gaikwad was removed soon after, though a stubborn 44-run stand between Ishan Kishan (27) and Axar Patel (21), alongside a rapid 21 from Naman Dhir, prevented India from suffering a record-breaking run defeat. Henry claimed three further victims to wrap up the innings, bowling India out for their sixth-lowest total in ODI history. Will Young celebrating hitting a century off 88 balls (Getty) At the start of the day, opener Young recovered from earlier scores of 9 and 6 in the series to make a career-best 125 off 108 balls to the gall of India who dropped him twice on the way to registering his fifth century in the format. The 33-year-old capitalised on sloppy Indian fielding after Rohit and Kishan dropped catches off consecutive balls during the second over of the innings. Young received solid support from Tim Seifert, who scored 58, and Finn Allen, who added 41, while India's bowling attack saw Patel, Gurnoor Brar and Auqib Nabi take two wickets apiece. item.description: Jun 11, 2026; Lake Forest, IL, USA; Chicago Bears quarterback Caleb Williams (18) speaks during Minicamp at Halas Hall. © Kamil Krzaczynski-Imagn Images Caleb Williams has established himself as the face of the Chicago Bears, but FS1 commentator Nick Wright isn’t completely sold on the hype. During Thursday’s episode of his What’s Wright podcast, Wright discussed Williams’ season so far. “For a player that was being discussed as the potential league MVP six days ago, he does have eight touchdowns and five picks. That’s where he is. … So I’m still super high on him, but you’ve gone up against three super elite defenses this year. Seattle, you won that handily. The Vikings, they stole your lunch money. And the Bucs, they took your lunch money, too. “We’ve got to be honest about the year he’s having up to this point. … He’s played six games. Four of them he was excellent, and two of them he was downright awful.” Williams completed just 15 passes for 138 yards and an interception in a 9-3 loss against Minnesota in September. On Sunday, the quarterback recorded twice as many interceptions (4) as passing touchdowns (2) in a 27-24 win over the Tampa Bay Buccaneers. Former NFL head coach Jon Gruden had a similar notion to Wright. He warned the former No. 1 pick about his interception problem during his appearance on Wake Up Barstool on Monday: “We all know you’re not going to win a Super Bowl or a championship turning the ball over at that rate,” Gruden said. Jeffery Simmons on Caleb Williams’ mistakes Caleb Williams is receiving feedback from within his own roster about his turnover problem. Defensive tackle Jeffery Simmons downplayed the severity of the turnovers: “It’s one of the things where I didn’t panic because Caleb is a baller,” he told reporters after the win against Tampa Bay. “He’s a gamer. Who cares? I mean, we all care, and I’m sure he cares about the turnovers. But one thing I told Caleb, we got his back. And just like at the end of the game when we really needed to get down into field goal range, he did his part. … He made plays that needed to be made, and that’s going to be the rest of the season.” Williams and the Bears are currently in their bye week. They return to action against the New Orleans Saints on Nov. 22. Kickoff is at 12 p.m. CT on Fox. The former nine-time Pro Bowler and nine-time All Pro selection served as Prescott’s starting guard for the first nine seasons of his career (2016-2024). Martin was arguably the best offensive lineman of the 2010s and was a model of consistency, playing his first four full seasons without missing a game.
